stories.headline: Death Valley’s Scotty’s Castle reopens for limited tours 11 years after flood
stories.title: Death Valley’s Scotty’s Castle reopens for limited tours 11 years after flood
stories.summary: More than a decade after a flash flood forced Scotty’s Castle to close, Death Valley National Park is bringing visitors back for limited exterior tours from October 10 as a $71 million restoration effort continues.
reasons: corroboration: single independent source -> medium confidence
article_sentences: Tours are scheduled for most Saturdays and Sundays through April 17, while private weekday tours can also be arranged for small groups.
The castle itself remains under restoration and is not yet reopening for regular interior visits.
The limited access marks another step in a recovery effort that has stretched for more than 10 years and is expected to continue for at least another two.
Scotty’s Castle has been closed since October 2015, when an extraordinary storm hit the northern part of Death Valley.
On October 18, the area received 2.75 inches of rain in about five hours, roughly equivalent to a typical year’s rainfall there.
Another half-inch had fallen the previous day.
Water, mud and rocks rushed through Grapevine Canyon in a flash flood estimated to be flowing at about 3,200 cubic feet per second.
The flood damaged buildings, utilities, historic landscaping and roads.
Much of the eight-mile Bonnie Clare Road leading toward Scotty’s Castle was destroyed.
More than 20 power poles were washed away, sections of the water and sewer systems were damaged and mud and rocks piled several feet deep around some buildings.
The National Park Service estimates that the overall repair effort costs about $71 million, with work divided across numerous projects and funding sources.

stories.headline: ED Moves Supreme Court Against Delhi HC Order Quashing Money Laundering Case Against NewsClick & Prabir Purkayastha
stories.title: ED Moves Supreme Court Against Delhi HC Order Quashing Money Laundering Case Against NewsClick & Prabir Purkayastha
reasons: corroboration: single independent source -> medium confidence
event term: 'supreme court' in title weight 44
article_sentences: The Enforcement Directorate (ED) has approached the Supreme Court challenging the Delhi High Court's decision to quash the FIR registered against digital news portal NewsClick and its founder-editor Prabir Purkayastha over alleged irregularities in foreign funding.

In a judgment delivered on May 29, Justice Neena Bansal Krishna of the Delhi High Court quashed the FIR registered by the Delhi Police's Economic Offences Wing (EOW) and the connected money laundering proceedings initiated by the ED, holding that the continuation of the proceedings amounted to a gross abuse of the process of law.
The High Court had found that the allegations did not disclose the commission of the offences invoked in the FIR and that the proceedings were not legally sustainable.
The FIR, registered in August 2020, invoked Sections 406 (criminal breach of trust), 420 (cheating) and 120B (criminal conspiracy) of the Indian Penal Code.

The case arose from allegations concerning foreign direct investment (FDI) received by PPK Newsclick Studio Private Limited, the company operating NewsClick, from US-based Worldwide Media Holdings LLC.

The investigating agency had alleged that the investment was structured to circumvent restrictions governing foreign investment in digital news media and that a portion of the funds was diverted towards salaries, consultancy fees, rent and other expenses.

The ED subsequently registered an Enforcement Case Information Report (ECIR) under the Prevention of Money Laundering Act (PMLA), treating the alleged offences in the FIR as the predicate offences for its investigation.
Rejecting the allegations, the High Court held that the material on record did not establish the commission of the alleged scheduled offences.
It also observed that the allegations concerning the share valuation and expenditure of the company did not, by themselves, establish criminal wrongdoing.
The Court further held that once the predicate FIR was quashed, the connected money laundering proceedings could not survive.
The ED's challenge before the Supreme Court seeks to overturn the High Court's decision.

The proceedings quashed by the High Court are separate from the UAPA case registered by the Delhi Police's Special Cell against NewsClick and Purkayastha over allegations relating to foreign funding and a purported conspiracy.

stories.headline: Haryana Cabinet approves continuation of Sixth Finance Commission recommendations
stories.title: Haryana Cabinet approves continuation of Sixth Finance Commission recommendations
stories.summary: The decision has been taken as the Seventh Finance Commission has not yet submitted its report to the government.
reasons: corroboration: single independent source -> medium confidence
event term: 'cabinet approves' in title weight 44
article_sentences: The decision has been taken as the Seventh Finance Commission has not yet submitted its report to the government.

Chandigarh: The Haryana Cabinet, presided over by Chief Minister Nayab Singh Saini here on Saturday, approved the continuation of the recommendations of the Sixth State Finance Commission for the devolution of funds to rural and urban local bodies from 2026-27 until the recommendations of the next Finance Commission come into force.

Accordingly, as per the established precedent, the approved recommendations of the Sixth State Finance Commission will continue to serve as the basis for the distribution of funds to local bodies during this period.
Under the approved framework, seven per cent of the state’s Own Tax Revenue (SOTR), on an actual basis, will be devolved to local bodies.
The distribution of funds to Gram Panchayats and Urban Local Bodies will be based on a weightage of 80 per cent for population and 20 per cent for area.
For Zila Parishads and Panchayat Samitis, the distribution will also be based on population data available on the Parivar Pehchan Patra Portal as of December 31 of each year.
The ‘inter-se’ distribution among Gram Panchayats, Panchayat Samitis and Zila Parishads will be maintained in the ratio of 75:15:10, respectively.
As per the approved framework, the local bodies will be permitted to utilise not more than 30 per cent of the devolved funds for pavement of streets.
The framework also stipulates that the actual revenue of Urban Local Bodies must be at least 85 per cent of their budgeted revenue, as reflected in the audited accounts of the previous year.
In case of non-compliance, the Urban Local Bodies concerned will face a 20 per cent reduction in their recommended share of the state Finance Commission grant due to them in the current year.

The Cabinet also approved key amendments to the Deen Dayal Lado Lakshmi Yojana to extend the benefits of the scheme to more eligible women, simplify its implementation and strengthen the delivery of financial assistance.
Under the approved amendments, the annual family income eligibility limit under the scheme will be increased from Rs 1 lakh to Rs 1.80 lakh.

stories.headline: Future military power will be defined by speed of sensing, understanding, deciding and acting: Rajnath Singh
stories.title: Future military power will be defined by speed of sensing, understanding, deciding and acting: Rajnath Singh
stories.summary: New Delhi, Oct 10: Defence Minister Rajnath Singh addressed the participants of the second edition of Exercise Tarang Shakti 2026 at Air Force Station Jodhpur on October 10, 2026. Hosted by the Indian Air Force (IAF) from 26 September to 12 October 2026, the multinational air exercise brought together air forces from seven Friendly Foreign Countries (FFCs) including Australia, Bangladesh, France, Germany, Sri Lanka, the United Arab Emirates and the United States of America along with 32 observer nations. Congratulating the IAF and all organisations and personnel involved in the successful conduct of the exercise, the Defence Minister welcomed the participating nations and appreciated their contribution to strengthening professional understanding and operational cooperation. He noted that the presence of participating air forces had added significant value to the exercise and expressed hope that the contingents would return with valuable professional insights and a deeper understanding of India's capabilities and perspectives. He highlighted the importance of self-reliance in the defence sector, technological innovation and international partnerships in addressing the evolving challenges of modern warfare. Addressing the gathering, Defence Minister Rajnath Singh observed that modern warfare was undergoing a profound transformation, extending beyond the traditional domains of land, sea and air to encompass space, cyber, the electromagnetic spectrum and the information domain. He highlighted the growing influence of unmanned systems, drones, artificial intelligence, electronic warfare and long-range precision weapons in shaping contemporary military operations. “Future military power will be defined less by the number of platforms we possess. It will be determined by the speed of sensing, understanding, deciding, and acting,” he said, underlining that speed, precision, information and integration had emerged as defining attributes of military capability. He also emphasised the need for continuous vigilance in view of the rapidly changing geopolitical environment and the uncertainties associated with technological advancements in the defence sector. The Defence Minister said that India, under the leadership of Prime Minister Narendra Modi, had recognised the importance of strengthening national resilience against emerging security challenges and had adopted Atmanirbharta in defence as a national policy. He stressed that a nation must possess the capability to produce its own weapons and critical technologies to sustain itself during prolonged conflicts and periods of uncertainty. Highlighting the transformation of the Indian Defence Forces, Defence Minister said that the Indian Air Force had evolved from a force operating with limited resources at the time of Independence into a modern aerospace power equipped with advanced aircraft, precision weapons, sophisticated sensors, integrated networks and increasingly advanced indigenous technologies. He emphasised that Atmanirbhar Bharat did not mean isolation from the world, but the development of domestic capabilities to design, develop, manufacture, maintain and upgrade critical defence technologies. Referring to India's growing aerospace and defence manufacturing ecosystem, the Defence Minister highlighted indigenous programmes and systems, including the Tejas fighter aircraft, helicopters such as Dhruv, Rudra, Prachand and the Light Utility Helicopter (LUH), the Akash air defence system, AESA radars, electronic systems, and emerging unmanned and aerospace technologies. Defence Minister also referred to the Advanced Medium Combat Aircraft (AMCA) programme as an important step towards mastering fifth-generation stealth fighter technology and underscored the importance of advanced aero-engine development and co-production. He said that India was keen to explore cooperation with like-minded countries in research, co-development, co-production, maintenance, training and innovation. Emphasising the growing importance of trusted partnerships and resilient supply chains, he stated, “The defence relationships of the future will be about technology and trust, not just about platforms.” The Defence Minister observed that building strong indigenous capabilities must go hand in hand with meaningful cooperation with trusted partners. India must be capable of acting independently when required while also operating effectively with other nations when their interests and responsibilities converge, he emphasised. In this context, Defence Minister highlighted the significance of Exercise Tarang Shakti in translating the principles of capability, technology, interoperability and trust into operational experience. The exercise provided participating air forces an opportunity to operate alongside one another, exchange operational knowledge, assess procedures and understand different platforms, doctrines and approaches to mission planning. He noted that multinational exercises enabled aircrews and commanders to learn from one another, examine existing assumptions and identify opportunities to improve their systems and processes. Describing the spirit of the exercise, Defence Minister Rajnath Singh said, “Different nations. Different aircraft. Different experiences. But one sky. That is the message of Tarang Shakti.” He emphasised that the value of the exercise extended beyond the sorties flown and scenarios practised, encompassing the ability to communicate, coordinate and operate effectively with partner forces. The RM called upon the Indian Air Force to incorporate the lessons of the exercise into its training, tactics, technology, doctrine and future capability development. He expressed confidence that the participating nations would carry forward the professional relationships and mutual understanding developed during the exercise to explore new avenues of aerospace and defence cooperation. The second edition of Exercise Tarang Shakti builds on the success of its inaugural edition in 2024 and reinforces India's commitment to constructive defence engagement and international cooperation. The exercise brought together diverse combat, transport, surveillance and air-to-air refuelling capabilities, providing opportunities for joint mission planning, operational learning and enhanced interoperability. The participation of indigenous platforms, including the Light Combat Aircraft (LCA) Tejas and the Light Combat Helicopter (LCH) Prachand, also highlighted India's progress in indigenous aerospace design, engineering and manufacturing. The contemporary relevance of the exercise is underscored by the decisive role of air power in Operation Sindoor, which demonstrated the Indian Air Force’s ability to execute precise, calibrated and effective operations in furtherance of national security objectives. The operation highlighted the importance of operational preparedness, integrated planning, credible deterrence and the effective application of air power in a complex security environment. The experience gained from operational employment reinforces the value of multinational exercises such as Tarang Shakti in advancing professional understanding and preparing for the evolving challenges of modern warfare. Beyond flying operations, the exercise featured professional engagements, industrial visits and cultural interactions, including yoga sessions, heritage visits and an International Night celebrating the traditions of participating nations. Chief of Defence Staff General N. S. Raja Subramani, Chief of the Air Staff, Air Chief Marshal A P Singh, Chief of the Naval Staff, Admiral Krishna Swaminathan, other dignitaries, officials of the Ministry of Defence and participating countries attended the event.

He noted that the presence of participating air forces had added significant value to the exercise and expressed hope that the contingents would return with valuable professional insights and a deeper understanding of India's capabilities and perspectives.
He highlighted the importance of self-reliance in the defence sector, technological innovation and international partnerships in addressing the evolving challenges of modern warfare.

Addressing the gathering, Defence Minister Rajnath Singh observed that modern warfare was undergoing a profound transformation, extending beyond the traditional domains of land, sea and air to encompass space, cyber, the electromagnetic spectrum and the information domain.
He highlighted the growing influence of unmanned systems, drones, artificial intelligence, electronic warfare and long-range precision weapons in shaping contemporary military operations.
“Future military power will be defined less by the number of platforms we possess.

It will be determined by the speed of sensing, understanding, deciding, and acting,” he said, underlining that speed, precision, information and integration had emerged as defining attributes of military capability.
He also emphasised the need for continuous vigilance in view of the rapidly changing geopolitical environment and the uncertainties associated with technological advancements in the defence sector.

The Defence Minister said that India, under the leadership of Prime Minister Narendra Modi, had recognised the importance of strengthening national resilience against emerging security challenges and had adopted Atmanirbharta in defence as a national policy.
He stressed that a nation must possess the capability to produce its own weapons and critical technologies to sustain itself during prolonged conflicts and periods of uncertainty.

Highlighting the transformation of the Indian Defence Forces, Defence Minister said that the Indian Air Force had evolved from a force operating with limited resources at the time of Independence into a modern aerospace power equipped with advanced aircraft, precision weapons, sophisticated sensors, integrated networks and increasingly advanced indigenous technologies.

He emphasised that Atmanirbhar Bharat did not mean isolation from the world, but the development of domestic capabilities to design, develop, manufacture, maintain and upgrade critical defence technologies.

Referring to India's growing aerospace and defence manufacturing ecosystem, the Defence Minister highlighted indigenous programmes and systems, including the Tejas fighter aircraft, helicopters such as Dhruv, Rudra, Prachand and the Light Utility Helicopter (LUH), the Akash air defence system, AESA radars, electronic systems, and emerging unmanned and aerospace technologies.

Defence Minister also referred to the Advanced Medium Combat Aircraft (AMCA) programme as an important step towards mastering fifth-generation stealth fighter technology and underscored the importance of advanced aero-engine development and co-production.
He said that India was keen to explore cooperation with like-minded countries in research, co-development, co-production, maintenance, training and innovation.

Emphasising the growing importance of trusted partnerships and resilient supply chains, he stated, “The defence relationships of the future will be about technology and trust, not just about platforms.” The Defence Minister observed that building strong indigenous capabilities must go hand in hand with meaningful cooperation with trusted partners.
India must be capable of acting independently when required while also operating effectively with other nations when their interests and responsibilities converge, he emphasised.

In this context, Defence Minister highlighted the significance of Exercise Tarang Shakti in translating the principles of capability, technology, interoperability and trust into operational experience.

The exercise provided participating air forces an opportunity to operate alongside one another, exchange operational knowledge, assess procedures and understand different platforms, doctrines and approaches to mission planning.
He noted that multinational exercises enabled aircrews and commanders to learn from one another, examine existing assumptions and identify opportunities to improve their systems and processes.
Describing the spirit of the exercise, Defence Minister Rajnath Singh said, “Different nations.
Different aircraft.
Different experiences.
But one sky.

That is the message of Tarang Shakti.” He emphasised that the value of the exercise extended beyond the sorties flown and scenarios practised, encompassing the ability to communicate, coordinate and operate effectively with partner forces.
The RM called upon the Indian Air Force to incorporate the lessons of the exercise into its training, tactics, technology, doctrine and future capability development.

He expressed confidence that the participating nations would carry forward the professional relationships and mutual understanding developed during the exercise to explore new avenues of aerospace and defence cooperation.
The second edition of Exercise Tarang Shakti builds on the success of its inaugural edition in 2024 and reinforces India's commitment to constructive defence engagement and international cooperation.

The exercise brought together diverse combat, transport, surveillance and air-to-air refuelling capabilities, providing opportunities for joint mission planning, operational learning and enhanced interoperability.

The participation of indigenous platforms, including the Light Combat Aircraft (LCA) Tejas and the Light Combat Helicopter (LCH) Prachand, also highlighted India's progress in indigenous aerospace design, engineering and manufacturing.

The contemporary relevance of the exercise is underscored by the decisive role of air power in Operation Sindoor, which demonstrated the Indian Air Force’s ability to execute precise, calibrated and effective operations in furtherance of national security objectives.
The operation highlighted the importance of operational preparedness, integrated planning, credible deterrence and the effective application of air power in a complex security environment.

The experience gained from operational employment reinforces the value of multinational exercises such as Tarang Shakti in advancing professional understanding and preparing for the evolving challenges of modern warfare.

Beyond flying operations, the exercise featured professional engagements, industrial visits and cultural interactions, including yoga sessions, heritage visits and an International Night celebrating the traditions of participating nations.
Chief of Defence Staff General N. S. Raja Subramani, Chief of the Air Staff, Air Chief Marshal.
A P Singh, Chief of the Naval Staff, Admiral Krishna Swaminathan, other dignitaries, officials of the Ministry of Defence and participating countries attended the event.
